column7: Line 115 is `group: release-${{ github.ref }}-1` while the Phase 2 job at line 477 uses `group: release-${{ github.ref }}-2`, and both set `cancel-in-progress: false`, so the two phases live in distinct concurrency groups and can never cancel each other.

Spec line 99 is `    else return endpoint_error (with diagnostics)` in an illustrative pseudocode sketch that already states (lines 85-88) `AbortSignal.any keeps the job's own abort signal authoritative`; the shipped implementation checks `if (signal.aborted) return outcome('cancelled');` before classifying (src/harness/adapter.ts:140), so the sketch is merely imprecise, not a defect.

Line 110 reads `  60-step job cannot accumulate 180 retries; the wall-clock and budget caps` and line 170 `  (default worst case ≈ 3 × (timeout or backoff) per step).` — the wording is loose, but this is a design document whose numbers do not affect any code path, and the adjacent text already states the wall-clock cap bounds the total.

Line 124 `- **Telemetry:** failed attempts log to the worker log via the existing` is ambiguous about which channel is meant, but 'step-callback channel' plainly denotes the worker-log path and the implementation resolved it unambiguously with `console.warn` in `logFailedAttempt` (src/harness/adapter.ts:277-279), so no contract is actually broken.

Both producers of the hook's error, `pickFromLibrary` and `captureFromCamera`, call `setError(null)` before awaiting the picker/camera, so an identical repeat failure is a real null -> same-string transition and the ref-guarded effect does fire again; the claim that photoError stays unchanged does not hold in this code.

Line 17-19 use `const id = Crypto.randomUUID();` to name the directory, so two concurrent calls get distinct `export-<uuid>` paths and there is no shared `exportDir` to collide on; `create({ idempotent: true })` further tolerates a collision.

At bd74a9b, SkiaGraphCanvas.tsx:51 reads `color={hashColor(node.okfType ?? node.id, dark)}` and line 21 computes `const dark = useColorScheme() === 'dark';`, so the dark flag IS passed and the claimed light-mode-in-dark-theme failure cannot occur.

graphData.ts:44 declares `export function hashColor(seed: string, dark = false)` and every call site at b3ea1df (SkiaGraphCanvas.tsx:48, GraphLegend.tsx:33) passes `dark` explicitly, so the signature change was propagated and no node renders with the wrong lightness.

Line 5 is `export function createMockLlmProvider(): LLMProvider {`; the whole file is a pure factory returning an object with a single async `generateText` that returns strings — it contains no subscription, no battery-state listener, and nothing to remove, so the claimed leak does not exist.

`_cached_section = None` is a module-level cache written only from the single-threaded Hermes plugin host, and a single-object assignment is atomic in CPython, so no torn or partially-written read is possible; the reported line 45 is in fact a blank line.

Line 42 reads `- uses: actions/cache@v4` while lines 28/32/34 pin actions/checkout, pnpm/action-setup and actions/setup-node to full SHAs, so the observation is factually correct but is a supply-chain-hardening preference rather than a functional defect; the tag reference works and the workflow is not broken by it.

Line 4 is '### Features' directly under the H1 release heading '# [5.4.0](...)', so markdownlint MD001 is technically triggered, but the file is a machine-generated changelog and 5.3.0 below uses the same H1 form, so this is a cosmetic generated-output nit with no functional impact.

Line 6 does contain 'closes [hi#effort](https://github.com/hi/issues/effort) [body-#-Citations](https://github.com/body-/issues/-Citations)' pointing at other repos, but this is generated changelog text derived from commit-message trailers in an auto-generated file, so it is documentation cosmetics rather than a defect a reviewer should block on.

`if len(groups) != 1:` -> `die(f"mixed providers among selected runs ...")` — rejecting mixed (provider, model) sets is the documented E8 design (module docstring lines 13-14 and the check's own docstring: 'One (provider, model) per sweep; mixed providers = hard error'), not an incorrect gate, and single-provider test data does not make the branch unreachable or wrong.

`precision = tp / denom if denom > 0 else (1.0 if recall == 1.0 else 0.0)` — every division on the empty-judged path is guarded (`recall = tp / golden_n if golden_n else 0.0`, the denom check, `if precision + recall > 0 else 0.0`, and `fp_neg_mean = sum(fp_neg_each) / len(fp_neg_each)` with len>=3 enforced by select_runs), so an empty `judged` list cannot raise ZeroDivisionError.
